senses.definition: Aware of something and visibly taking it into account when a decision is made.
senses.caution: A memo word, not a spoken one. Said aloud it sounds stiff and aware would do the same job, but in writing it earns its place because it puts on record that you knew and weighed something, which is exactly what an auditor or a regulator is reading for. Be careful claiming it after the fact about a risk you plainly missed, and note that a large IT services firm carries the name, so in a vendor conversation there will be a beat where someone thinks you meant them.
senses.example: We are cognizant of the concentration risk, and the phased rollout is the answer to it.

cues.text: You are drafting a paper and want a formal way to record that the team already weighed the risk the committee is about to raise.
A regulator asks whether the implications were understood at the time, and they were.
Writing to a landlord about a repair, you want to acknowledge that he has other tenants without sounding casual about your own problem.
Explaining a decision to a family member, you want a slightly formal way of saying their situation was in view the whole way through.

distractors: Told about something after the decision has already been made.
Able to explain a subject clearly to someone who has never met it.
Responsible for a piece of work and answerable for how it turns out.
Kept informed of progress at regular intervals without being asked to approve anything.
Trained in a procedure well enough to carry it out without checking the manual first.
